CORRECTED this round: the original variants ("CC=NO", "CC(=NO)") were the same structure written twice with a redundant parenthesis, not a real tautomer pair -- not a valid fixture at all. Real pair (nitrosoethane / acetaldehyde oxime, RDKit-formula-verified C2H5NO both) is CONFIRMED FAILING on main (99401a6): canonical_tautomer("CCN=O") stays C(C)N=O, canonical_tautomer("CC=NO") stays ON=CC. Root cause is distinct from the aromatic gap (RFC section 1.6): the one matching rule, "1,3-C-to-O-any-bridge", is marked prefer_forward:false (likely deliberately, to avoid enolizing plain ketones via the same any-bridge pattern), so it never fires in either direction from canonical_tautomer's loop.

phenol has an exocyclic O on an aromatic ring, superficially similar to the lactam/lactim class (tp2-05..09), but has no lactam-like mobile-H partner -- canonical_tautomer(Oc1ccccc1) must stay c1(O)ccccc1 (aromatic phenol), never get pushed toward a cyclohexadienone form. Currently passes (correctly a no-op); exists to catch over-eager matching once round 2C implements the section 4.4 aromatic-shift generalization.

anisole has no mobile H anywhere in the molecule (the O bears no H, it's fully substituted); canonical_tautomer must be a strict no-op. Currently passes; guards against round 2C's fix inventing a transfer where none is chemically possible.

aniline has an exocyclic N on an aromatic ring, the nitrogen analog of tp2-25's phenol concern; canonical_tautomer must stay aromatic aniline (Nc1ccccc1), never get pushed toward an exocyclic-imine/cyclohexadiene-imine form. Currently passes; guards round 2C the same way as tp2-25.

pyridine N-oxide has an exocyclic O directly on an aromatic-ring heteroatom, structurally adjacent to the lactam/lactim class but chemically distinct: the O carries the formal negative charge (n+/O- zwitterionic N-oxide), not a mobile H. Must not be reinterpreted as a lactam/lactim system by round 2C's fix. Currently passes (c1ccc[n+]([O-])c1, unchanged).
